messages:
jamal: Noticing weirdness in the latency dashboard: rollup p50 is lower than the endpoint p50 for /v2/complete, but p95/p99 at endpoint are higher. Graphs look inverted depending on the view. Anyone seen reservoir sampling artifacts like this?

maria: I've seen something similar when rollups aggregate tdigest summaries from shards with different sample rates. The merged tdigest can bias the median if one shard has very few samples.

alejandro: Could be compounded by our retry de-dup logic. If retry samples are deduped at the endpoint view but not at the rollup ingestion, counts differ by view which changes the percentile calculation.

jamal: Quick check: I pulled the rollup metadata for the 10:00-10:10 window and counts look odd.
```text
rollup shard A: samples=1200, tdigest_centroids=85
rollup shard B: samples=8, tdigest_centroids=4
merge result: samples=1208, p50=45ms
endpoint raw: samples=1192, p50=78ms
```

jamal: Shard B's tiny sample push pulls the merged tdigest toward the lower bucket in this case.

tess: That matches a hypothesis i had: small ephemeral clients (mobile ad-hoc) can produce narrow latency tails, and when their sparse tdigest merges in, median shifts. But endpoint view filters them earlier.

oncall-jen: This is a known caveat of hierarchical tdigest-based rollups. We added a note in the ingestion docs but it's not surfaced in the console.

sara-product: From a UX/SLO perspective, we should not surprise users: the median disagreement needs a provenance callout and maybe an explanation tooltip. Product would prefer a clear "Rollup vs Endpoint" badge.

maria: Two engineering options: 1) increase reservoir/sample floor per shard before including its tdigest in merges (drop shards with samples < N), or 2) emit per-shard counts in the rollup metadata and compute weighted percentiles at query time (expensive). Both have tradeoffs.

alejandro: Another cheap heuristic: when merging tdigests, if any child shard has samples < 50, tag the merged rollup as "low-confidence" for p50 and above. Console can then grey or annotate the tile.

jamal: Agree. Short-term I can add a rollup flag at ingestion: low_sample_warning=true when any contributing shard sample_count < 50. That won't change numbers but gives visibility.

tess: Can we also make the console default to showing endpoint-level p50 when users have a route selected? Rollup is useful for overview, but when drilling into a single route I'd expect endpoint numbers.

sara-product: Yes, default drilldown behavior should prefer the most precise view (endpoint) and show rollup as an overlay. We'll draft UX text for the badge: "Rollup may include low-sample shards; see details."

oncall-jen: Operational note: we need to ensure this flag is computed cheaply in the aggregator. It's just a min(sample_count) check across children. Low compute cost.

jamal: I'll open an infra PR to emit the low_sample_warning boolean and include a small JSON snippet with contributing_shard_counts for debugging.

maria: For the longer term, consider switching rollups to keep both merged-tdigest and raw-sample-count-distributions for critical routes (SLO endpoints). It's more storage but solves correctness for SLOs.

alejandro: Also add a quick query we can run from console to surface disagreement windows. I used this one:
```sql
SELECT hour, rollup.p50 AS rollup_p50, endpoint.p50 AS endpoint_p50, rollup.meta.min_child_samples
FROM latency_rollups rollup
JOIN latency_endpoints endpoint USING (route, hour)
WHERE route='/v2/complete' AND hour BETWEEN '2026-03-15T10:00' AND '2026-03-15T11:00'
ORDER BY hour;
```

jamal: Nice. I'll wire the low_sample_warning into the rollup docs and add a console badge that links to the query.

tess: UX piccolo: badge states "low-sample rollup" with hover text and an action to "Prefer endpoint". Can we add that before EOD as a feature flag?

sara-product: We can ship a feature-flagged change to the console for quick rollout. Product ok with that plan.

oncall-jen: deploy-bot: note a small change to aggregator schema will be needed; schedule a canary.

deploy-bot: :warning: deploy 2026-03-25T15:40Z planned aggregator: add-rollup-low-sample-flag (id: aggr-4421)

jamal: I'll coordinate the PR and test with synthetic shards to validate the flag flips correctly.

maria: Also, let's add a short runbook for oncall: when you see rollup/endpoint divergence, run the query, check min_child_samples, and open an infra ticket if min_child_samples < 50 for many consecutive windows.

alejandro: Thanks all. This should reduce surprise for customers and give us clear engineering levers (floor, per-route retention) for critical SLOs.

-- end of thread --
